programme.title: The Elegance of Luoyang
programme.desc: Luoyang, as the eastern starting point of the Silk Road, is a city with a rich history and a tradition of cultural inclusivity. As such, it enjoys a prominent position in the heritage of the whole world.\nIn this episode, we’ll visit White Horse Temple to learn about its fascinating international background. At Longmen Grottoes, which were designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the year 2000, we’ll appreciate how the unique ancient splendor is being revived by 3D technology. At the city’s annual Peony Festival, we’ll explore the significance of China’s national flower and national dress.\nInvited to a Luoyang Water Banquet, we’ll learn something about the city’s culinary traditions. And finally, a master of tang sancai, or tri-color pottery, will discuss the legacy of this ancient craft and its place in the modern era.

programme.title: The sound of casting
programme.desc: For centuries, the fires of craftsmanship have never faded in Pingyao. In this UNESCO World Heritage city once famed for trade, three ancient metalworking traditions — sword casting, gold and silver crafting, and iron forging — continue to thrive. This episode steps into the workshops where artisans shape metal with fire and devotion. Each blade’s edge, each ornament’s gleam, and each curve of wrought iron tells a story of resilience and artistry — revealing how the spirit of Pingyao’s craftsmanship still glows in the heart of time.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker’s Guide to China: Mount Siguniang
programme.desc: In this episode, Host Tianran He is on a mission: To reach the summit of Mount Siguniang, a towering snowcapped mountain in southwestern China. Together with his friend Ma Chunlin, a photographer for National Geographic, they trek through one of China’s most beautiful and biodiverse hiking routes, before making for base camp. But with worsening weather conditions and severe altitude sickness, the odds are stacked against them. Ten years ago, Tianran failed his attempt at climbing Mount Siguniang’s First Peak – this time, he’s all in.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker’s Guide to China: Changbai Mountain
programme.desc: An unforgettable adventure awaits amidst the breathtaking landscapes of Changbai Mountain! Embark on a trek through pristine birch forests, marvel at the majestic power of the world's deepest volcanic waterfall, and uncover hidden gems along the way. Indulge in soaking in natural hot springs and experience exhilarating rafting down mountain streams, all leading to the final destination: Tianchi Lake, a heavenly oasis nestled in the clouds. Join the Travelogue team as we delve into the beauty of Changbai Mountain.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.1
programme.desc: Lhasa, set high on the “Roof of the World” in China’s southwest, is both the capital of Xizang Autonomous Region, and the spiritual heart of Tibetan culture. In this episode, host Tianran He ventures deep into the fabled Potala Palace, discovering ancient meditation caves, priceless relics and golden rooftops. Then, he tries his hand at Tibetan papermaking, learning how a poisonous ingredient is crucial for making paper that can survive for centuries. Finally, Tianran dons his apron and learns to make iconic Tibetan dishes, including one said to reveal your fortune.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.2
programme.desc: Tianran He explores Lhasa’s bustling Barkhor Street, where pilgrims, locals, and visitors alike circle its ancient lanes. This multicultural district, home to sacred temples and boutique shops, becomes the backdrop as Tianran dons traditional Tibetan attire for a photoshoot. Across the city, he meets high school students dancing for Douyin — China’s version of TikTok, blending street dance with traditional Tibetan moves. Finally, Tianran travels to the birthplace of Tibetan incense, where waterwheels still power this thousand-year-old craft.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.5
programme.desc: Guarded by mountains in southeast China, Jiangxi channels rivers into Poyang Lake---the Yangtze's vital link. Starting from Mount Lu's misty slopes, watch and marvel as northern plains transition into an undulating land of hills and basins..

programme.title: Quanzhou Nanyin: A Living Fossil in the History of Chinese Music
programme.desc: Nanyin, also known as “Quanzhou Nanyin,” is an ancient Han Chinese musical tradition whose singing style preserves the time-honored ethnic vocal techniques predating the Tang Dynasty, earning it the title of “a living fossil in the history of Chinese music.”\nThe program features Yegor, a Ukrainian music enthusiast, visiting Master Su Shuyong, a Nanyin inheritor, to hear her decades-long stories of teaching this art. They also tour the Quanzhou Nanyin Troupe, where, led by its artistic director Zhuang Lifen, they learn about the basic performance formats and instruments of Nanyin. Additionally, the episode follows a post-1990s Nanyin performer, Zheng Mingming, as she sips tea with guests at sunset, reflecting on the deep-rooted role Nanyin plays in the daily lives of Quanzhou’s people.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.3
programme.desc: Join Tianran He on a high-speed train to Shigatse, gateway to the Himalayas and home to Mount Qomolangma, the world’s highest peak. As the city with the most land ports in Xizang, Shigatse serves as a key corridor to South Asia. Here, Tianran samples breakfast at a bustling local teahouse and experiences monastic life at the vast Tashilunpo Monastery. He then visits an agricultural park where tropical crops thrive against the odds of the alpine plateau, before discovering pulu — a traditional Tibetan textile now earning global acclaim.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He travels to Shannan, the cradle of Tibetan culture. Nestled in the gentlest valley of the Yarlung Zangbo River, this is where the first Tibetan king rose to power, the first palace in Xizang was built, and many other “firsts” in Xizang’s history began. Tianran visits Yamdrok Lake, one of Xizang’s three sacred lakes, where a paragliding base is taking shape. He then learns the art of Tibetan opera, joins rangers on a mission to track the elusive Tibetan red deer, and ends the day with a rejuvenating soak in a village revitalized by hot spring tourism.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.5
programme.desc: In this final episode, Tianran journeys to Nyingchi, known as “Xizang’s Garden.” Here, he experiences the region’s semi-pastoral way of life — feeding yaks, trying his hand at archery, and seeing how tourism is transforming lives in Lulang International Tourist Town. Travelling along National Highway 318, Tianran discovers towering millennia-old cypress trees and rafts through the vast Yani National Wetland Park, before ending the day with a unique spa treatment at a traditional Tibetan hospital.

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media – Changsha was China's first UNESCO \"Creative City\". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. \nThe soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: Ding Porcelain Firing
programme.desc:
In ancient times, skilled craftsmen combined clay with fire and, using nothing more than their hands and wisdom, created the history of porcelain.

A thousand years ago, at the time of the Northern Song Dynasty, a type of porcelain was produced that stood out for its exquisite quality, elegant coloring and beautiful patterns. This was Ding porcelain, and it became a favorite at the imperial court. However, within 200 years, amid the chaos of constant warfare, the art of making it was lost. The dazzling white light of the Ding kilns had faded, seemingly forever. 

And yet, 800 years later, that light has been reignited.

programme.title: From Stone to Story
programme.desc: China's profound stone carving culture dates back to the Han Dynasty (202 BC – 220 AD) and flourished during the Tang Dynasty (618 – 907 AD), evolving into a distinctive art form and unique cultural practice. Among many places famous for stone carving, Hui’an County—through generations of dedicated artisans—has risen to prominence and earned the esteemed title of \"World Capital of Stone Carving,\" awarded by the World Crafts Council.\nThe county’s skilled stonemasons are celebrated for their ability to transform ordinary pieces of rock into beautiful works of art. This episode shines a spotlight on the intangible cultural heritage of Hui’an stone carving and reveals how it has been influenced by the area’s close proximity to the sea.

programme.title: Crossroads of Cultures: The Legacy of Silk Roads
programme.desc:
Quanzhou, situated on the southeastern coast of China, once served as a maritime hub of the East and Southeast Asia trade network during the 10th to 14th centuries, gaining prominence for its exceptional trading port.
With 22 distinctive heritage sites listed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, this city stands as a testament to the legendary history of the Silk Roads.
In this program, we invite four individuals living in Quanzhou to showcase their daily lives, capturing their journeys through the city's world heritage sites.
Through their perspectives, we present a dynamic portrayal of a city rich in heritage. From the maritime splendor of Quanzhou's history to the serene echoes of its ancient city, from the historical treasures of the Luoyang Bridge to the vibrancy of the modern urban landscape, we journey alongside our guests through time and space, exploring Quanzhou's diverse charm and unique allure. Join us as we immerse ourselves in a city that bridges history and cultures, and embraces innovation.

programme.title: World Heritage in China: Ancient City of Pingyao
programme.desc: Established in the 14th century, Pingyao retains the typical layout of the county-level cities of the Han people in Central China. The ancient city is a complete community comprising walls, streets and lanes, shops, houses and temples.?As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Pingyao remains a testament to traditional Chinese urban planning and architecture, attracting visitors from around the world who seek to explore its historical streets and vibrant history.

programme.title: Jingmai Wanderings: A Symphony of Humans and Tea
programme.desc: As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Mount Jingmai embodies the ecological wisdom of forest–tea symbiosis and the rich cultural diversity of its ethnic communities. It plays a vital role in biodiversity conservation and the preservation of traditional tea culture.\nThis episode follows the stories of representative individuals to explore three key themes — heritage preservation, ecological sustainability, and youth empowerment — revealing the unique charm and sustainable development model of Mount Jingmai.

The ancient city is a complete community comprising walls, streets and lanes, shops, houses and temples.?As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Pingyao remains a testament to traditional Chinese urban planning and architecture, attracting visitors from around the world who seek to explore its historical streets and vibrant history.

programme.title: Jingmai Wanderings: A Symphony of Humans and Tea
programme.desc: As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Mount Jingmai embodies the ecological wisdom of forest–tea symbiosis and the rich cultural diversity of its ethnic communities. It plays a vital role in biodiversity conservation and the preservation of traditional tea culture.\nThis episode follows the stories of representative individuals to explore three key themes — heritage preservation, ecological sustainability, and youth empowerment — revealing the unique charm and sustainable development model of Mount Jingmai.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.3
programme.desc: Join Tianran He on a high-speed train to Shigatse, gateway to the Himalayas and home to Mount Qomolangma, the world’s highest peak. As the city with the most land ports in Xizang, Shigatse serves as a key corridor to South Asia. Here, Tianran samples breakfast at a bustling local teahouse and experiences monastic life at the vast Tashilunpo Monastery. He then visits an agricultural park where tropical crops thrive against the odds of the alpine plateau, before discovering pulu — a traditional Tibetan textile now earning global acclaim.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He travels to Shannan, the cradle of Tibetan culture. Nestled in the gentlest valley of the Yarlung Zangbo River, this is where the first Tibetan king rose to power, the first palace in Xizang was built, and many other “firsts” in Xizang’s history began. Tianran visits Yamdrok Lake, one of Xizang’s three sacred lakes, where a paragliding base is taking shape. He then learns the art of Tibetan opera, joins rangers on a mission to track the elusive Tibetan red deer, and ends the day with a rejuvenating soak in a village revitalized by hot spring tourism.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.5
programme.desc: In this final episode, Tianran journeys to Nyingchi, known as “Xizang’s Garden.” Here, he experiences the region’s semi-pastoral way of life — feeding yaks, trying his hand at archery, and seeing how tourism is transforming lives in Lulang International Tourist Town. Travelling along National Highway 318, Tianran discovers towering millennia-old cypress trees and rafts through the vast Yani National Wetland Park, before ending the day with a unique spa treatment at a traditional Tibetan hospital.

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media – Changsha was China's first UNESCO \"Creative City\". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. \nThe soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: Aerial China:Beijing
programme.desc: China’s capital of Beijing is a bucket list city for any self-styled world traveler, but let’s be honest, not all of us have the time! Not to worry, because we’re about to embark on an aerial journey over the nation’s heart, giving you a crash course on this massive hub of culture, international exchange, and technological innovation. If you’re afraid of heights, this may be the one time it’s okay to look down.

programme.title: Ding Porcelain Firing
programme.desc:
In ancient times, skilled craftsmen combined clay with fire and, using nothing more than their hands and wisdom, created the history of porcelain.

A thousand years ago, at the time of the Northern Song Dynasty, a type of porcelain was produced that stood out for its exquisite quality, elegant coloring and beautiful patterns. This was Ding porcelain, and it became a favorite at the imperial court. However, within 200 years, amid the chaos of constant warfare, the art of making it was lost. The dazzling white light of the Ding kilns had faded, seemingly forever. 

And yet, 800 years later, that light has been reignited.

programme.title: From Stone to Story
programme.desc: China's profound stone carving culture dates back to the Han Dynasty (202 BC – 220 AD) and flourished during the Tang Dynasty (618 – 907 AD), evolving into a distinctive art form and unique cultural practice. Among many places famous for stone carving, Hui’an County—through generations of dedicated artisans—has risen to prominence and earned the esteemed title of \"World Capital of Stone Carving,\" awarded by the World Crafts Council.\nThe county’s skilled stonemasons are celebrated for their ability to transform ordinary pieces of rock into beautiful works of art. This episode shines a spotlight on the intangible cultural heritage of Hui’an stone carving and reveals how it has been influenced by the area’s close proximity to the sea.

programme.title: Crossroads of Cultures: The Legacy of Silk Roads
programme.desc:
Quanzhou, situated on the southeastern coast of China, once served as a maritime hub of the East and Southeast Asia trade network during the 10th to 14th centuries, gaining prominence for its exceptional trading port.
With 22 distinctive heritage sites listed on the UNESCO World Heritage List, this city stands as a testament to the legendary history of the Silk Roads.
In this program, we invite four individuals living in Quanzhou to showcase their daily lives, capturing their journeys through the city's world heritage sites.
Through their perspectives, we present a dynamic portrayal of a city rich in heritage. From the maritime splendor of Quanzhou's history to the serene echoes of its ancient city, from the historical treasures of the Luoyang Bridge to the vibrancy of the modern urban landscape, we journey alongside our guests through time and space, exploring Quanzhou's diverse charm and unique allure. Join us as we immerse ourselves in a city that bridges history and cultures, and embraces innovation.

programme.title: China Bound：Xiamen
programme.desc: What's it like in one of China's happiest cities? Tianran is in sunny Xiamen on China's southeast coast, visiting the city's famous \"island of music\" and sampling local delicacies like shark meatballs, shacha noodles and fish in \"soy sauce water\". He'll discover former fishing villages turned hipster havens, drink tea with locals beneath traditional tenement buildings, and visit a student enclave brimming with creative startup energy.

programme.title: China Bound：Suzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He visits Suzhou, a historic city in eastern China famously admired by Marco Polo. Crisscrossed by canals, Suzhou is renowned for its exquisite gardens, where ancient scholars recreated nature's beauty within their own homes. Tianran discovers a city of refined tastes, where even a bowl of breakfast noodles comes with unspoken etiquette, locals insist on only in-season produce, and foodies eagerly await the arrival of prized hairy crabs.

programme.title: China Bound: Chengdu
programme.desc: Tianran spends 3 days in Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan Province and UNESCO's first City of Gastronomy. He dives deep into Chengdu culture, exploring the infamous \"mala\" numbing and spicy flavors of Sichuanese street food and hotpot, and visiting historical attractions like Wuhou Shrine, Du Fu's Thatched Cottage, and the Jinsha Site Museum, which houses exquisite relics from a 3,000-year-old kingdom uncovered beneath the streets of Chengdu. Of course, no visit to this city is complete without seeing giant pandas and enjoying a cup of tea while getting your ears cleaned in the iconic People's Park. After all, when in Chengdu, do as the locals do.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China : Shanghai
programme.desc: Balancing delicately on an alluvial plain and the Yangtze estuary of China’s east coast, much of Shanghai-literally meaning “on the sea”-sits at an average sea-level elevation of about 4 meters. Bisecting the city is the Huangpu River, dividing it into Puxi (west bank) and Pudong (east bank), where you’ll find its famous international airport. Join us as on an aerial cruise as we journey upstream towards one of the world’s most recognizable skylines.

programme.title: Suzhou Fans
programme.desc: Suzhou, known as the “Venice of China,” is also famous for its traditional crafts. And one of the most elegant and exquisite crafts is Suzhou fans. Celebrated for their exquisite design and fine quality, they’re popularly associated with literati. How come Suzhou gave birth to such a variety of fans? How can we appreciate their beauty in the modern world? In this episode, we are discovering more stories behind Suzhou fans.

programme.title: Seafaring Tales: Fu Ships
programme.desc: In past centuries, transporting goods along the Maritime Silk Road could be a hazardous undertaking. Ships often faced fierce storms which blew up on the high seas. To reduce the danger, China’s shipbuilders came up with a solution. They developed Fu ships, commonly known as junks, incorporating a special watertight bulkhead technology. Their revolutionary design allowed the ships to withstand the highest winds and roughest waters.\nThe Maritime Silk Road was an ancient trading route that connected China to Southeast and South Asia, the Middle East, and Africa. As a key passageway for trade and cultural exchange, it thrived for well over a thousand years, bringing Chinese tea, silk, porcelain, spices, and other precious cargo to the rest of the planet. The legacy of the Maritime Silk Road is still evident today in many parts of the world.

programme.title: Yangliuqing New Year Painting Art
programme.desc: On May 20, 2006, Yangliuqing New Year Paintings were named as part of China’s national intangible cultural heritage. The New Year painting tradition can be traced back many centuries, to the Ming Dynasty and beyond, reaching the height of its popularity in the Qing Dynasty. There are no restrictions on the themes of the paintings, and there is no blessing they cannot convey. Yangliuqing New Year Paintings are loved all over the country for their beautiful details and vivid colors—but most of all, for the good wishes they impart to anyone who sees them.

programme.title: Quanzhou Nanyin: A Living Fossil in the History of Chinese Music
programme.desc: Nanyin, also known as “Quanzhou Nanyin,” is an ancient Han Chinese musical tradition whose singing style preserves the time-honored ethnic vocal techniques predating the Tang Dynasty, earning it the title of “a living fossil in the history of Chinese music.”\nThe program features Yegor, a Ukrainian music enthusiast, visiting Master Su Shuyong, a Nanyin inheritor, to hear her decades-long stories of teaching this art. They also tour the Quanzhou Nanyin Troupe, where, led by its artistic director Zhuang Lifen, they learn about the basic performance formats and instruments of Nanyin. Additionally, the episode follows a post-1990s Nanyin performer, Zheng Mingming, as she sips tea with guests at sunset, reflecting on the deep-rooted role Nanyin plays in the daily lives of Quanzhou’s people.
